description: If a dentist is not careful during removal of your child's lower wisdom teeth, damage to the lingual or inferior alveolar nerves can result.
shortAnswer: If a dentist is not careful during removal of your child's lower wisdom teeth, nerve damage can result. Damage to the lingual nerves can result in anesthesia (numb tongue), paresthesia (tingling), or dysesthesia (pain and burning) in the tongue and inner mucous membranes of the mouth, and the loss of the ability to taste.

faq.q: What is the inferior alveolar nerve and how can it be injured?
faq.a: The inferior alveolar nerves (sometimes also called inferior dental nerves) connect the brain to the chin, lower lip, and jaw. They can be injured by tooth extractions, root canals, and the placement of implants.

faq.q: How can nerve damage from wisdom tooth removal affect my child?
faq.a: These types of injury may affect your child's appearance, his/her ability to speak, drink and eat. Loss of sensation in the tongue may make it difficult for your child to know what they are eating (and when it is time to swallow) and may alter how food tastes to your child.

faq.q: Can lingual nerve damage from a tooth extraction be repaired?
faq.a: Corrective surgery is available but may or may not be successful. One procedure involves taking a nerve from your child's foot or ankle to try to repair the damaged oral nerves. If surgical repair fails, your child may be left with permanent nerve damage.
